about: The chat fluidity budgets (chat programme A5; design/chat-vs-slack/perf-mobile.md PM-1 to PM-7; G-CHAT-PERF). scripts/fluidity/chat.mjs measures each on a production build against the fake server side (fakeApp.mjs): a synthetic workspace of six channels, one of them 2,000 messages long and paged as the server pages it, and three DMs, at 150 ms a round trip. It exits non-zero when an enforced value is over its max. Each value is the median of the runs; a switch's figures are the p95 of its twelve switches a run.

target is perf-mobile.md's first target (after A1 and A5), and owner the package that gets it there. measured is the first run, on 17 Oct 2026 (beta 7397fab2c with the shell diet): at 1x with the machine quiet (load 2 to 12), at 4x under load (46 to 53), which inflates the 4x times.

Where a value is over target, max is that measure with room for a shared machine (about 25 to 30%, rounded); where it is under, max is the target. Renders hold at any CPU speed, so they gate on a busy machine where the times don't.

The read-back pulls the way the list loads (CHAT-LEAD, 17 Oct): a real scroll event within 200 px of the top while the list isn't busy (aria-busy), nudged when already at the top. Six pulls fetch six older pages of 50 (350 rows).
Never raise a max to make a run pass. Lower it when a package brings a metric down, and to the target once the metric holds there.

20 Oct 2026 (FLUIDITY-LEAD, fluid-04): a thread opened from the long channel and typed in. The long channel's messages show their threads (a reply row with faces on every ninth, 40 replies each); the five short channels the switches visit don't, so the switch budgets still compare with 17 Oct. heapMB is taken before the thread, as before.

network.why: As the doc budgets: the low end of the demo's time to first byte.

coldOpenMs.source: A channel opened in a fresh tab until its first message row shows. Demo, 13 Oct: 2.2-2.5 s at 1x, 3.4-4.9 s at 4x. First target 1.5 s on a computer, 3.5 s on a mid phone

switchP95Ms.source: Twelve switches through the sidebar (channel, channel, DM ...), click to the first new row, the p95. Demo, 13 Oct: p90 558-688 ms at 1x, 839-1,209 at 4x. First target 200 ms at 1x, 500 at 4x; later 100 and 300

rendersPerSwitch.source: React renders per switch, the median of the run's twelve: 3,546 at 1x and 3,194 at 4x on 17 Oct (about 3,700 on the demo): the whole list re-renders. What a 200 ms switch needs gone

switchCls.source: Layout shift during a switch, the p95. 0 on the fixtures; 0.13 on the demo's open and switch on 17 Oct, which the fixtures' even rows don't reproduce yet

keyP95Ms.source: A sentence typed in the composer, the per-key p95. 24 ms at 1x and 136 ms at 4x on 17 Oct

scrollOlderPages.source: Six pulls to the top of the 2,000-message channel: the older pages fetched. Six on 17 Oct, one a pull. Report only: the fixture pages 50 at a time, as A1's exact cursors will, while the server pages 10 today (domain/Post/postDomain.go, PM-4), so the count says nothing about the server's paging until A1 moves it; enforce it then, with the fixture at the server's page size

scrollTbtMs.source: Blocking time while reading back those 300 messages, at 1x: 4,314 ms on 17 Oct at load 38 (the rows each page brings render at once). perf-mobile.md: no task over 100 ms

heapMB.source: JS heap at the run's end, after the switches and the read-back of 350 rows: 65 MB on 17 Oct (51 MB when the read-back fetched one page; 28-44 MB on the demo's short channels, PM-7). First target 60 MB

threadOpenMs.source: 'N replies' clicked in the long channel until the thread panel draws its replies (40). Beta 482460c3d on fixtures, 20 Oct 2026, P-cores, median of 5: 489.0 at 1x on a computer. Times above load 16 are inflated: provisional until a quiet rerun. Target: Instant: an open or switch from cache within 100 ms on a computer (the brief's bar; Nielsen's 0.1 s limit for 'instantaneous'; RAIL's 100 ms response), and 300 ms on the 4x phone profile (the chat programme's later 4x target, perf-mobile.md)

threadOpenRenders.source: Renders to open a 40-reply thread from a settled list (the chip scrolled into view, then the list left 1.5 s: it says it stopped scrolling 1.2 s after the last scroll). Beta 482460c3d on fixtures, 20 Oct 2026, P-cores, median of 5: 22544 at 1x on a computer, 8,383 of them the channel's rows remounting (the virtual list kept overscan only ahead of a scroll, so the rows behind one mounted afresh when it stopped). With CHAT-LEAD's keepMounted (web 9e8230b77, 21 Oct): 2560 in each of 3 runs (profiling build, P-core, load about 20): the panel's own mount (about 1,160), the list re-laid at the panel's width (about 700), the composer. Target: render only what changed (the fluidity method: rows memoised on id-only props, a window of the rows on screen)

threadKeyP95Ms.source: A reply typed in the thread's composer: the key p95. Beta 482460c3d on fixtures, 20 Oct 2026, P-cores, median of 5: 24.0 at 1x on a computer. Times above load 16 are inflated: provisional until a quiet rerun. Target: Key p95: a keystroke paints within two frames, 32 ms at 1x and 50 ms at 4x (docs I20, doc-budgets.json)

channelEmptyMounts.source: A conversation that has messages draws its empty state ("This is the start of #…", the fill placement) while it opens: the render where the first read's answer has come but the list's store is still empty (CHAT-LEAD, 21 Oct 2026; DESIGN-BUILD-3 saw its fade under the composer at 390). Counted by its arrivals in the page, the cold open and every switch, each run's worst open, median of runs. Live batch 4 (4b30ac377), 21 Oct 2026 (FLUIDITY-LEAD-6): 2 an open at 1x and on the phone at 4x. Target: never (0); report only until it reads 0
